newsitem.title: USA: US May spot gas prices little changed, trade thin.
newsitem.headline: US May spot gas prices little changed, trade thin.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices for May were little changed Tuesday, but with bidweek deadlines now over, many were sidelined waiting for May flows to begin on Thursday, industry sources said.
Despite prospects for steady storage buying, many expected May to start on a soft note, citing seasonal weather forecasts that promised little heating or cooling demand near-term.

"I don't think there's much in the way of weather for the first two weeks of May, but prices could move up later as you pick up some cooling demand," said one East Coast trader, noting May Gulf Coast prices still in the $2.04-09/mmBtu range.
April gas at the Gulf was steady to up slightly, with the Hub talked at $2.10 or better, as players sought supplies for last minute balancing.
In south Texas, early May notionally firmed slightly to near the $2.05 area, helped by warm weather in the region.

Midwest quotes for May notionally lost a couple of cents to the low-$1.90s on early-month forecasts for seasonal to slightly-below seasonal temperatures that offered little chance for heating loads. April Midcon gas was steady to down slightly in the low-$1.90s.

In the Northeast, early May gas in New York eased a few cents to the mid-to-high $2.30s on expected mild weather in the region. Appalachian prices for next month lost similar ground to the low-$2.30s.
At the Chicago city-gate, May held steady at around $2.17.
In west Texas, Permian prices were unchanged in the mid-to-high $1.80s. Southern California border gas for May also was flat in the high-$1.90s.
